approach:
Count the rejected, failed or timed-out jobs in one retry lineage (a chain of "try again on <job>" requests) from the job records. The count is built on `job_history` and `retries_by_job` in `crates/athena-core/src/reading/retry.rs`, with a named constant `LINEAGE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT = 3`. `lineage_stop` returns None when the job is in no lineage or has fewer than 3 failed attempts. Otherwise it returns the failed job ids, the findings and unmet criteria that repeated across at least two attempts, and a `NarrowerAction`: Queued(existing marker request), Queue(text of a new narrower request) or Refused(reason).

Round-3 change (finding 1): "repeated" is decided with the codebase's own T4 comparison, not exact string equality. Unmet criteria use `scope_guard::compare_criteria`, which lowercases, drops digits, collapses whitespace and matches by equality, containment or more than half shared words (scope_guard.rs:189-220); a result of Yes or Maybe is a repeat. Blocker and major findings repeat when their location paths match with `:line[:col]` stripped and `compare_criteria` on their summaries is Yes or Maybe. A finding with no location needs a Yes. Contrasting pairs are tested.

The narrower request is defined mechanically, not as a renamed retry. Its title is `Re-scope or split <root>: <first repeated item>`. Its acceptance bullets are only the repeated unmet criteria and one bullet per repeated blocker or major finding, capped strictly below the root's bullet count when the root has several. Leftover repeated items go in the body under "Left for a later request". Its files come from the repeated findings' locations, kept to the root's files when they overlap, then the root's files, then the fallback `StewardRequest::from_change` already uses. A request that is itself a narrower request never gets another: `lineage_stop` returns Refused, the drain still stops, and the operator decides.

The drain asks through two new `Steps` methods with defaults, so no existing implementor changes. It asks at two places in `Drain::attempts`: (1) the loop top before `run_job`, for a non-landing attempt; (2) right after `failures += 1`, before the `failures >= ATTEMPTS` return. A hand `athena retry` stays unlimited.

A new `lineage-limit` default is added to `defaults.toml`. The reader set is at 1997 of 2000 and the new line costs about 20 tokens, so something must leave the reader view. Updating the facts line cannot absorb it (1997 plus about 20 is over 2000, and the facts file says update the line, never the budget). `buy-first` is therefore split at its real `; ` break, which saves exactly the bytes the new line adds. The change is stated openly as a change to what the reader sees.

decisions.choice:
Ask `Steps::lineage_stop` at two points in `Drain::attempts` (drain.rs:1855-1957) through one helper `Drain::lineage_end(item, job) -> Option<ItemEnd>`. Point 1: inside `if passed.is_none()` after the `paused_reason` check (1875-1877) and before `run_job` (1887), with `last_job`. Point 2: right after `failures += 1` (1941), only when `passed.is_none()` and `paused_reason(item)` is None, before the `failures >= ATTEMPTS` block (1942). The helper calls `lineage_stop`, then `queue_narrower` (skipped for Refused), writes one `drain      <item> stopped: ...` UI line plus a `note_once`, and returns `ItemEnd::LineageStopped(reason)`; `finish` passes the item over with the reason. A landing retry of a passed job (`passed.is_some()`) is not a new attempt and is not checked.
   Which test needs which point (corrected, finding 2). Point 2 runs after EVERY failure, not only the last one, so the two points overlap. (a) A queued retry item whose chain already holds 3 failures: nothing has failed in the item yet, so only point 1 can stop it before it is read and run; without point 1 the item is read, run, and only then stopped by point 2, so q is no longer Queued. (b) A lineage that becomes 3 on the item's second in-run attempt: `failures` becomes 2 and the function returns `Failed` (1951-1954) at once, so only point 2 sees it; without point 2 no narrower request is queued and the output says `failed twice`. (c) A lineage that becomes 3 on the item's first in-run attempt (the in-item test, q is the 3rd failure): point 2 stops it at failures == 1, and if point 2 were missing, point 1 at the next loop top would stop it. This test therefore fails only when both points are removed. It shows no 4th attempt, but does not discriminate a single point. The queued-retry test discriminates point 1 and the second-attempt test discriminates point 2.
decisions.reason: Point 1 covers a queued retry item whose chain is already at 3 and any retry after a failure. Point 2 covers the lineage that reaches 3 on the item's last in-run attempt, which returns Failed before the loop top. The pause keeps priority, so the scope guard's own stop is unchanged.

rejected.why: Misses the lineage that reaches 3 on the item's second in-run attempt: it returns `ItemEnd::Failed` first with no narrower request.
Misses a queued retry item that is already at 3 before its first read; it would be read and run once more.
It would also block the operator's own `athena retry`, the manual override, and the drain would see an error rather than a stop it can answer with a narrower request.

decisions.choice: `lineage_attempts(records, job)` in retry.rs calls `job_history` once and derives the forward map with a private `retries_in(records, &history)` that `retries_by_job` is changed to call (same result). It returns empty at once when the job has no `retry_of` and no entry in the forward map. Otherwise it walks forward to the newest standing retry, then back along `retry_of`, with a seen-set and `MAX_RETRY_DEPTH` each way, and keeps jobs whose `records.jobs[id].state()` is Closed(Rejected | Failed | TimedOut), oldest first. `pub const LINEAGE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT: usize = 3`.

decisions.choice:
The replacement is an ordinary request built by `StewardRequest::new` and queued with `Athena::queue` (channel `cli`). Title: `Re-scope or split <root id>: <first repeated item, one line, at most 80 characters>`. Body: starts `Lineage <root id>: failed attempts <ids>.`, then the repeated findings (one line each, length-capped), then `Left for a later request:` for repeated items that did not fit. Acceptance: one bullet per repeated unmet criterion (`Meet: <criterion>`) and per repeated blocker/major finding (`Resolve: <summary>`), at most max(1, root bullets - 1) of them when the root has more than one bullet; never the root's full list.
   How a repeat is decided (finding 1, replaces exact equality). Work on the structured data, not the formatted `finding_text` line: each failed attempt's final verification gives its unmet criteria (criterion text) and its blocker/major findings (`finding_blocks`; `Finding.summary`, `Finding.location`). Helpers in retry.rs: `location_path(loc)` strips trailing `:line` and `:line:col` segments; `same_criterion(a, b)` is `scope_guard::compare_criteria(a, b)` not `No` and neither text empty (so case, digits and whitespace do not matter, and containment or more than half shared words counts); `same_finding(a, b)` is true when both are located with equal paths and `same_criterion` holds on the summaries, or when either is unlocated and `compare_criteria` on the summaries is exactly `Yes`. Items are clustered across attempts in order: the first sighting starts a cluster, each later attempt joins the first cluster it matches, and a cluster counts each attempt at most once. A cluster in at least 2 failed attempts is repeated, and the text shown is the latest attempt's wording (so line numbers are current). A failed attempt with no verification contributes its closing reason line as an item. If nothing repeats, the last attempt's blocking findings are used and the body says none repeated.
   Files: (1) paths from the repeated findings' `location` (path with `:line[:col]` stripped, `looks_like_path`), restricted to the root's `request_text_touches` when that overlap is non-empty; (2) else the root's touches; (3) else `records/`, the fallback `StewardRequest::from_change` already uses (steward.rs:624-630). `lineage_stop` finds an existing request job whose text contains `Lineage <root id>:` and returns Queued(it), so later passes queue nothing. If the lineage root's own request starts with `Re-scope or split `, the action is Refused and nothing is queued.
decisions.reason: Fresh verifier runs write free-text summaries and locations with line numbers, so only the normalised comparison the scope guard already trusts for T4 (scope_guard.rs:189-220) can find repeats in real lineages. `StewardRequest::new` checks the text against the parse `athena plan` uses (steward.rs:532-592) and demands at least one bullet and one path (560-567), which the three-step files fallback guarantees. The narrowing is checkable: acceptance differs from the root's text and is no larger than its bullet count, strictly smaller when the root has several. The second-generation stop closes the loop that a fresh lineage at zero would otherwise open. `queue` redacts and commits a Request record on the already-drained `cli` channel. No new record type, so `check_record_file` and `AnyRecord` are untouched. Maybe counts as a repeat because the cost of a false repeat is one extra bullet in a smaller request, and the scope guard itself treats Maybe as worth a flag.

rejected.why: Rarely matches across independent verifier runs, so the request would almost always say nothing repeated (critic finding 1).
Misses reworded findings, the realistic case; Yes needs identical text after normalising, which is exact equality apart from case and digits.

demonstrations.method: Three tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs over `drain::drain(&real_steps(&athena, &lander), limits, &Lines)` with a `Scenario` whose verdict is `fail` with every criterion met and one major finding `the description lists no callers` (a Fail verdict or blocking finding gives final_verdict Fail, verify.rs:649-672; no unmet criterion, so the scope guard's T4 does not pause). (A) `a_lineage_with_three_rejected_attempts_gets_no_fourth_attempt`: run j1 by hand to Rejected; `athena.retry(j1)` and run it to Rejected j2; `athena.queue("try again on <j2>")` = q. Drain with `max_jobs: 2`. The drain reads and runs q (the 3rd failure). Assert: j1, j2 and q are `JobState::Closed(OutcomeState::Rejected)`; `lineage_attempts(&records, q)` is exactly [j1, j2, q]; no request job has text `try again on <q>`; `steps.paused(&[q])` is empty; the lander landed nothing for q; the `drain      <q> stopped:` or `plan       <q> passed over:` line names the lineage stop; no output line says `over the job limit` for q. (B) `a_queued_retry_of_a_lineage_with_three_failures_is_not_read_or_run`: hand-reject j1, j2 (`athena.retry`) and j3 (`athena.retry(j2)`), then `athena.queue("try again on <j3>")` = q; drain with `max_jobs: 2`. Assert q is still `JobState::Queued`, no job of q's own exists, no job has text `try again on <q>`, and the passed-over line names the lineage. Planning may read q, so the Reader count is not asserted. (C) `a_lineage_that_reaches_three_failures_on_the_items_second_attempt_queues_the_narrower_request` (see criterion 4).

open_questions: User: should a hand-run `athena retry` also stop at 3 failed attempts? The plan limits only the drain and keeps the manual command as the operator's override, because the request says Athena should stop retrying.
User: is counting a timed-out job as a failed attempt acceptable? The request says "rejected or failed"; the plan also counts timed-out, since `athena retry` and the drain treat the three alike.

User: the reader prompt has 3 tokens of room and the new default needs about 20, so some reader text must go. The plan shortens the reader's view of `buy-first` (producer and verifier still see all of it). Do you accept that, or name a different default to shorten? Do not choose to raise the 2000 budget; the facts file forbids it.
